pages.title: Metamaterial Sheet
pages.text: A material whose properties come from its structure rather than its chemistry: a lattice of resonators smaller than a wavelength, arranged to give it a negative refractive index. Light entering it bends the wrong way, and objects behind it look subtly turned inside out. The surface is iridescent and feels like fine woven fabric.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Metamaterial Weaver let me knot quantum dots and quartz into a neutronium plate at sub-wavelength spacing, with a condensate to keep everything in phase. The first sheet bent my lamp beam backwards and I spent an hour checking it was real.
